claude.sample_unit: questions (true/false, 5 runs per model); plus 10 dental students in pilot

links.outcome: Accuracy of LLMs with vs without RAG grounding in AHA guideline
links.effect: RAG effect varied by model: GPT-4o unchanged (78.6%); Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Gemini 1.5 Pro nonsignificantly decreased without preprompt; with preprompt gains for GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro, decline for Claude 3.5 Sonnet; none significant.
links.quote: RAG did not, however, universally enhance accuracy, occasionally leading to slight performance declines.

links.outcome: Student accuracy and time with vs without LLM assistance versus standalone LLM accuracy
links.effect: DeepSeek Reasoner (83.6% standalone) gave postgraduates nonsignificant gain (85.0% to 86.4%), undergraduates nonsignificant drop (82.9% to 79.3%); completion time rose 15.2 to 26.2 and 8.4 to 14.4 minutes.
links.quote: Moreover, a pilot user study demonstrated that LLM assistance provided no significant accuracy gains for dental students or postgraduates and increased task duration, highlighting practical limitations for current clinical integration.

links.outcome: Human performance with and without LLM assistance in intended deployment mode
links.effect: Postgraduate scores 85.0% to 86.4% (nonsignificant); undergraduates 82.9% to 79.3% (four of five decreased); all took longer with LLM.
links.quote: For undergraduate students, four out of five participants showed a decrease in their scores during the second round of the questionnaire, resulting in a nonsignificant drop from 82.9% ± 6.4 to 79.3% ± 4.67.

links.outcome: Response consistency across five repeated runs, with and without preprompt
links.effect: Consistency ranged 78.6-96.4%; Claude 3.7 Sonnet highest at 96.4% without preprompt; preprompting increased consistency for some models and decreased it for Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.3 70b, Grok 3 beta.
links.quote: Consistency increased for Claude 3.5 Sonnet, DeepSeek Reasoner, and GPT-o3-mini, but decreased for Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.3 70b, and Grok 3 beta.

links.outcome: LLM accuracy against ground-truth guideline answers for endocarditis prophylaxis
links.effect: Accuracy ranged from 42.1% (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) to 90.0% (Grok 3 beta with preprompt); authors conclude accuracy insufficient for unsupervised use.
links.quote: The findings of this study indicate that, although LLMs demonstrate potential, their accuracy remains insufficient for unsupervised use in patient care.

links.outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers that clinicians might act on without verification
links.effect: Best LLM accuracy 83.6-90%, lowest 42.1%; authors state LLM information on IE management should be independently verified before clinical use.
links.quote: The most important consideration is that, given IE is a life-threatening condition, information obtained from LLMs regarding patient management should always be independently verified before clinical application.

unlisted_practices: Preprompting ('You are an experienced dentist') to improve LLM accuracy
Considering response time/latency as co-primary metric alongside accuracy

openai.sample_unit: true/false IE prophylaxis questions; each queried across 10 LLMs, 2 prompts, 5 runs; pilot n=10 students

links.effect: No-preprompt accuracy ranged 42.1% ± 1.6 to 83.6% ± 3.2; preprompt top was 90.0% ± 3.0 and lowest 47.1% ± 1.6.
links.quote: The lowest accuracy was observed for Claude 3.7 Sonnet, at 42.1% without preprompts and 47.1% with preprompts.

links.effect: GPT-4o with RAG matched non-RAG at 78.6%; RAG caused nonsignificant decreases for Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Gemini 1.5 Pro, with mixed preprompt effects.
links.quote: RAG did not, however, universally enhance accuracy, occasionally leading to slight performance declines.

links.effect: Response consistency across five runs ranged from 82.1% to 96.4% without preprompt and 78.6% to 96.4% with preprompt; several models decreased with preprompting.
links.quote: Consistency increased for Claude 3.5 Sonnet, DeepSeek Reasoner, and GPT-o3-mini, but decreased for Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.3 70b, and Grok 3 beta.

links.effect: Postgraduate accuracy 85.0% ± 6.4 to 86.4% ± 6.4; undergraduate 82.9% ± 6.4 to 79.3% ± 4.67; times rose 15.2 to 26.2 and 8.4 to 14.4 minutes.
links.quote: Moreover, a pilot user study demonstrated that LLM assistance provided no significant accuracy gains for dental students or postgraduates and increased task duration, highlighting practical limitations for current clinical integration.

unlisted_practices: Using a role preprompt ('You are an experienced dentist.') to improve LLM accuracy for clinical questions

links.outcome: LLM accuracy with RAG versus non-RAG models
links.effect: RAG did not significantly enhance accuracy; without preprompt, GPT-4o matched baseline (78.6%), while Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Gemini 1.5 Pro decreased; with preprompt, gains for GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro were non-significant.
links.quote: Second, the hypotheses predicting a performance gain for LLMs using RAG and an enhancement in student performance were also not supported, as neither of these effects reached statistical significance.

links.outcome: human-AI team task accuracy and completion time
links.effect: LLM assistance did not significantly improve postgraduate accuracy (85.0% to 86.4%) and nonsignificantly decreased undergraduate accuracy (82.9% to 79.3%), while average completion times increased from 15.2 to 26.2 minutes and 8.4 to 14.4 minutes, respectively.
links.quote: Congruent with these mixed outcomes, our study showed that DeepSeek Reasoner, despite achieving the highest mean accuracy among LLMs without preprompting, provided negligible benefit to participants’ overall task performance.

unlisted_practices: Role-based persona preprompting ('You are an experienced dentist') to enhance LLM accuracy
